subject: AcreetionOS Update — July 01, 2026
body:
Recent updates to our continuous integration pipeline have significantly improved the reliability of our ISO build process, with changes such as per-pipeline staging directories to avoid publish races between concurrent builds, and the use of relative symlinks for the latest.iso file, ensuring it resolves correctly on the host web root. These tweaks may seem minor, but they have a major impact on the overall stability of our release process, which you can track on our changelog page at https://acreetionos.org/changelog.html.

Development
Our community has been actively refining the ISO build process, and the introduction of per-pipeline staging directories is a direct result of these efforts. This improvement will help avoid publish races between concurrent builds, ensuring that our releases are always up-to-date and reliable. You can learn more about our development process and how to get involved on our wiki page at https://acreetionos.org/wiki.html.

Community
The broader Linux ecosystem has also seen some exciting updates, including the release of Emacs 31.1 and the latest stable kernel set. Our community is always discussing the latest developments and how they impact AcreetionOS, and you can join the conversation on our forums. For more information on how to get started with AcreetionOS, check out our documentation page at https://acreetionos.org/docs.html. Tip of the day: if you're looking for the latest ISO image, you can always find it on our website at https://acreetionos.org/flash.html.
